summary: Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1986). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from approximately 2005 to 2024.

Seikaku Hirata worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1946–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, and also studied under Bokuo Seki. He later held a post at Hanazono University from around 1969 to 1994.

Seiki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. His academic career includes serving as an assistant at Kyoto University, an assistant professor at Shuchiin University, and an assistant professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).
Seiran Ouchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Totsudo Kato. He served as a lecturer (侍講) at Nishi Hongan-ji and was president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

Seiren Matsunami worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring (~1936–1939). He was a professor at Kyushu University (~1952–1967) and Rissho University (~1967–1974).

Seishi Karashima worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Cambridge, and Peking University. He held positions at Toho Kenkyukai and served as director/professor at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~1996–2019).

Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1888–1891) and Taisho University (~1891–1893). He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), Taisho University (1940), and Toyo University (1952, 1955).
Seitatsu Matsunami specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Seizan Yanagida was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Kaiten Nukariya, he held professorships at Hanazono, Kyoto, and Chubu universities, and directed the IRIZ.
Sen Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1932–1936), he served as a professor at Minzu University of China from around 1952 to 1964.

Senarat Wijayasundara worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University from around 1936 to 1937.

Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1935–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from approximately 1954 to 1978.

Sengaku Mayeda was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, and University of Münster. He held faculty posts at Pennsylvania, Tokyo, and Musashino University, and chaired Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.

Senkyo Sakawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Rissho University (completing studies in 1965) and served there as a professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985) and later professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Senmyo Naniwa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under P. V. Bapat, G. Sasaki, M. G. Dhadphale, and J. R. Joshi. In 2005, he was attested as a professor at Bukkyo University.
Sensho Kimura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University (~1962–1971) and later served as a professor there from around 1989 to 2009.

Sensho Murakami worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University, Higashi Honganji Kyoshi Gakko, and Toyo University, and later served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1917–1923) and lecturer at Otani University.
Sentaro Sawamura was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1907 to 1910 and later held a post there from approximately 1920 to 1930.
Seok-hyeong Kim worked in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University, he served as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.
